subject.title: [Feature] Prune stale orphaned sessions from Dashboard Sessions

question: Should OpenClaw add a Dashboard orphan-prune flow for Telegram/Discord sessions, and where should reachability ownership live?
rationale: The implementation is destructive and crosses Dashboard, session-store, protocol, and channel/plugin ownership boundaries, so automation should not pick default age, false-positive handling, or auto-prune policy on its own.

options.title: Approve manual preview/apply first
options.body: Add a Dashboard prune flow that previews eligible rows, asks channel/plugin reachability adapters to verify orphan status, revalidates before deletion, and leaves auto-prune for later.

options.title: Keep manual deletion only
options.body: Decline the new prune feature for now and rely on selected-row deletion plus generic sessions cleanup while preserving channel conversation rows by default.

options.title: Design auto-prune policy now
options.body: Broaden the work into a persistent per-session or per-channel auto-prune setting with migration, docs, and channel-specific safety rules.

recommendation.title: Approve manual preview/apply first
recommendation.body: Add a Dashboard prune flow that previews eligible rows, asks channel/plugin reachability adapters to verify orphan status, revalidates before deletion, and leaves auto-prune for later.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent broad session-management work makes this the best available routing candidate for the product boundary decision.
